title: The Salt Landfall
premise: Sable Oyelaran, a railroad engineer drifting along the empire's decommissioned coastal lines, is handed a dying prospector's map to the Meridian Star—a salvage wreck sunk in the Salt Flats—and a promise he must keep: deliver the man's share to a daughter he's never met. Hunted by the Vane salvage fleet and shadowed by the prospector's treacherous former partner, Sable must reach the wreck within six tides or lose it to the deep forever. Along the way he gathers an unlikely crew who become the family he never let himself want. In the end, Sable sacrifices his own escape route to save them, claims the wreck not for its gold but for the railroad charter hidden aboard, and finally stops running—building a life, and a line, on the salt.
about_author: Theo Nakamura is a former harbor surveyor who spent a decade mapping drowned coastlines before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people who build things in places that want to swallow them.

chapters.title: The Last Open Line
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Riding a rusted maintenance car down a closed coastal rail spur, Sable repairs track for food and keeps moving before anyone learns his name. A stationmaster offers him permanent work; he refuses by dawn. Emotional beat: the ache of chosen loneliness.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable finds prospector Ede Korrish gut-shot in a drainage culvert. Ede trades a wax-sealed map of the Meridian Star wreck for a promise: bring his share to his daughter Wren in Port Calloway. Emotional beat: guilt at accepting a burden he never asked for.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Studying the map over a cheap lamp, he calculates the tide tables: six tides until the wreck's air pocket floods and the fleet's sonar sweeps find it first. He decides to run—alone. Emotional beat: cold resolve masking fear.

chapters.title: Wren of Port Calloway
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In Port Calloway, Wren Korrish works a net-mending crew and waits for a father who always promised to come back. She recognizes Sable's hesitation when he asks about Ede. Emotional beat: hope sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Vane Fleet Weighs Anchor
chapters.summary: Vane POV (fleet captain Ilsa Vane). The salvage fleet launches early after a bribed harbormaster leaks word of a prospector's death. Ilsa burns Ede's old camp. Emotional beat: predatory patience.

chapters.title: Stowaway
chapters.summary: Sable discovers Wren hiding in his supply wagon, having pieced together her father's fate. He tries to leave her behind twice; both times she outmaneuvers him. Emotional beat: reluctant respect cracking his armor.

chapters.title: The Salt Flats Crossing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The wagon crosses the exposed flats at low tide, wheels sinking, a squall chasing them. Wren reads currents better than any chart. They barely beat the water back. Emotional beat: first flicker of trust.

chapters.title: The Partner
chapters.summary: Dess Corvane, Ede's former partner, intercepts them at a waystation, all charm and veiled threats, demanding half the map. Sable gives him a forged copy. Emotional beat: dread—he knows Dess won't stay fooled.

chapters.title: Tide Three: The Drowned Signal Box
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following the map through a flooded signal box on the old seabed line, Sable's engineering knowledge unlocks a mechanism Ede couldn't. Wren watches him work and sees her father's stories made real. Emotional beat: wonder.

chapters.title: Fleet on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. From a dune ridge they spot the Vane fleet's masts, a day ahead of schedule. Dess sold them out. Sable plans a decoy route; Wren insists on staying. Emotional beat: terror hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Decoy Line
chapters.summary: Sable reroutes a derelict locomotive as a false signal to pull two fleet cutters off their trail. It nearly kills him when the boiler lets go. Wren drags him clear. Emotional beat: she saves him—the debt reverses.

chapters.title: What Ede Never Said
chapters.summary: Around a driftwood fire, Wren shares letters revealing Ede wasn't hunting treasure but evidence: the Meridian Star carried a railroad charter proving the coastal lines were stolen from settler communities—including hers. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Tide Four: Betrayal at the Causeway
chapters.summary: Dess catches them at the causeway with hired blades. A brutal fight on the tidal causeway; Sable takes a knife wound, Dess escapes with the map's outer seal. But the inner coordinates live only in Sable's head. Emotional beat: cost written in blood.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Offer
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vane captures Wren during a supply raid and sends terms: the wreck's location for the girl. Sable's POV, alone with the choice he swore never to face again—run, or stand. Emotional beat: the old instinct to vanish versus something new.

chapters.title: Crew of the Stranded
chapters.summary: Sable rallies the flats' scattered denizens—a tide-pilot widow, deserting fleet stokers, the stationmaster from chapter one—to mount a rescue. For the first time he asks for help instead of paying for it. Emotional beat: found family assembling.

chapters.title: Tide Five: Storm Wall
chapters.summary: The rescue rides ahead of a storm wall into the fleet anchorage. Sable uses the drowned signal box's mechanisms to ground two cutters on sandbars while the crew extracts Wren. Emotional beat: audacity, and the joy of building something that works.

chapters.title: The Meridian Star
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With one tide left, they dive the wreck itself: the gold is real, but so is the charter, sealed in the captain's safe. Dess arrives, desperate, and Ilsa's flagship closes on the site. Emotional beat: awe curdling into siege.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: The Flood
chapters.summary: Climax begins. The final tide floods the wreck's air pocket as Dess and Ilsa's boarding parties converge inside the hull. Sable collapses a bulkhead to trap the boarders, saving Wren but sealing himself in the flooding section. Emotional beat: sacrifice as choice, not accident.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Believing Sable lost, Wren leads the crew out through the storm with the charter and Ede's share. Dess drowns grasping at gold; Ilsa retreats, her fleet crippled. Emotional beat: victory hollowed by grief.

chapters.title: The Man Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Sable survives via an emergency air lock he installed himself—an engineer's habit of building exits. He limps into Port Calloway three days later. Emotional beat: disbelief turning to homecoming.

chapters.title: Charter Day
chapters.summary: The charter is read publicly; the coastal lines are restored to the settler towns, and Sable is offered chief engineer of the rebuilt line. Ilsa, ruined, signs on as a rival salvager under new law rather than fight. Emotional beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: The Salt Landfall
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. One year later: the first train runs the restored coast road, Wren as stationmistress, Sble's maintenance car retired beside the platform. He plants a marker for Ede where the land meets the sea. Emotional beat: belonging earned, the price paid, the moving finally stopped.
